questions.stem: A car continuously covers a total distance of 600 km in exactly 12 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Speed = 600 km ÷ 12 hours = 50 km/h.

questions.stem: A young boy walks steadily at a speed of exactly 4 km/h. How much total time does he take to walk a distance of 20 km?
questions.explanation: Time = Distance ÷ Speed. Time = 20 km ÷ 4 km/h = 5 hours.

questions.stem: A train covers a certain distance in exactly 50 minutes if it runs at a speed of 48 km/h. The speed at which the train must run to reduce the time of the journey to exactly 40 minutes will be:
questions.explanation: First, find the distance. 50 minutes = 50/60 hours. Distance = Speed × Time = 48 × (50/60) = 40 km. Now, the new time is 40 minutes = 40/60 hours. New Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 40 ÷ (40/60) = (40 × 60) ÷ 40 = 60 km/h.

questions.stem: Excluding stoppages, the average speed of a bus is exactly 54 km/h, and including stoppages, it is 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the bus mathematically stop per hour?
questions.explanation: The loss in speed due to stopping is 54 - 45 = 9 km/h. This means the bus is not traveling 9 km out of the 54 km it could have traveled in an hour. The time taken to cover this 9 km at the original speed of 54 km/h is the stoppage time. Stoppage Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 9/54 hours = 1/6 hours. 1/6 of an hour = (1/6) × 60 minutes = 10 minutes.

questions.stem: A man completes a long journey in exactly 10 hours. He travels the first half of the journey at the rate of 21 km/h and the second half at the rate of 24 km/h. Find the total journey distance in km.
questions.explanation: Let the total distance be 2d, so each half is d. Time taken = (d/21) + (d/24) = 10 hours. LCM of 21 and 24 is 168. (8d + 7d) / 168 = 10. 15d / 168 = 10. 15d = 1680. d = 112 km. Total distance = 2d = 2 × 112 = 224 km.

questions.stem: Two men start together to consistently walk a certain distance, one at 4 km/h and another at 3 km/h. The former completely arrives half an hour before the latter. Find the exact distance.
questions.explanation: Let the distance be D km. The time taken by the slower man is D/3 hours and the faster man is D/4 hours. The difference in their times is exactly half an hour (1/2 hour). So, (D/3) - (D/4) = 1/2. Common denominator is 12: (4D - 3D) / 12 = 1/2. D / 12 = 1/2 => D = 6 km.

questions.stem: A thief is suddenly spotted by a policeman from a distance of exactly 100 metres. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 8 km/h and that of the policeman is 10 km/h, how far will the thief have physically run before he is overtaken?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 10 - 8 = 2 km/h. Distance to close = 100 metres = 0.1 km. Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 0.1 / 2 = 1/20 hours. In this 1/20 hours, the distance traveled by the thief = Speed of thief × Time = 8 × (1/20) = 8/20 km = 0.4 km = 400 metres.
